title: Ames and thesis 16+: Reformed admit preparatory dispositions
source_text: XLIX. Quam autem hoc non abhorreat a doctrina Reformatorum, patet ex iis quae ante docuimus Thesi 16. & sequentibus. Quibus conformia sunt quae satis prolixe disputat Amesius, Disput. Theologica de praeparatione peccatoris ad conversionem, quae subjuncta est ejus rescriptioni ad Nicolaum Grevinchovium, ubi disertis verbis Th. 3. asserit, in omni peccatore post usum rationis convertendo & regenerando, ex ordine praecedere dispositiones quasdam eo facientes, quamvis dispari gradu, secundum sa-pientiam dispensationis divinae.
pass_a_gloss: But how this does not clash with the doctrine of the Reformers appears from what we taught before in Thesis 16 and the following. Conformable to which are what Ames disputes at sufficient length in the Theological Disputation on the preparation of the sinner for conversion, which is subjoined to his reply to Nicolas Grevinchoven, where in express words in Thesis 3 he asserts that in every sinner to be converted and regenerated after the use of reason certain dispositions making for that end precede by order, though in unequal degree according to the wisdom of the divine dispensation.
pass_b_english: This does not clash with Reformed teaching from thesis 16 onward.
Ames: in every convert after reason's use, some dispositions ordinarily precede, in differing degrees.
